text: There are twenty-four built-in presets; a first painting still starts with Ink.
Test a few strokes, then favorite the presets you reach for.
The Chinese Liuye tool is Lasso fill in English, building color masses from closed shapes.
Draw a closed outline and release to fill it—ideal for petals and silhouettes.
The leaf-shaped tip follows the stroke, changing its width and pose as it turns.
Willow helps taper strokes and form leaves; it is separate from Lasso fill.
Change size and hardness to move from local edges to broad areas of color.
Then adjust spacing and paper texture to see how the marks settle.
Pressure affects size and opacity separately, with curves adjusted to your touch.
For repeating forms, enable symmetry and place the axis before painting.
Short smudge strokes push existing color; gentle mixing joins neighboring masses.
Pixel presets keep a distinct raster mode. Custom brushes can be saved and imported.
